bullets.title: Fed rate hike odds surge post-Warsh Jackson Hole speech
bullets.body: Warsh vowed to bring inflation back to target and warned inflation isn't 'meaningfully slowing,' sending 2-year Treasury yields up sharply—the largest one-day move since March 12—to 4.348%. Markets priced 57-60% odds of a September hike, with Barclays and Deutsche Bank both forecasting two 25bp hikes (Sep+Dec). One analyst noted the Fed's default may have flipped: data now must justify holding rather than hiking.

bullets.title: German Bund 10-year yield hits 15-year high; JGB yields surge too
bullets.body: Germany's 10-year yield reached 3.29%, a fresh 15-year high, while Japan's 2-year JGB yield hit 1.75%, the highest in 31+ years, driving a broad global rates reset. US Treasury Secretary Bessent called yen moves 'pretty well contained' and declined to advise the BOJ on rate hikes, while noting Ueda would 'do the right thing.'

bullets.title: Oil spikes on US-Iran military exchanges; Strait of Hormuz shipping disrupted
bullets.body: WTI rallied to ~$84.50-$85 and Brent above $90 after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island; Iran retaliated with ballistic missile attacks on US bases in Jordan. A supertanker was hit by mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and commodity ship traffic through Hormuz fell to five daily. Analysts note Persian Gulf oil flows have only recovered to ~40% of prewar levels (6-8M bpd).

bullets.title: Hedge funds sold most IT stocks in 2+ years; private client cash at record low 9%
bullets.body: Goldman data shows hedge funds cut IT exposure at the fastest pace in over two years the prior week. Separately, Bank of America Flow Show data shows private client cash allocation plunged to a record-low 9%, signaling extreme positioning. Goldman derivatives head noted the hawkish Jackson Hole pushed 10-year yields up 4bps intraday despite markets expecting the opposite.

bullets.title: BofA: NVDA 34-50% undervalued; $350 target; OpenAI Jalapeño chip poses longer-term threat
bullets.body: Bank of America sees NVDA as 34-50% undervalued with a $350 price target, citing the stock's discount partly reflects its backstopping up to $105B of residual value on OpenAI data center builds. Separately, commentary noted OpenAI's Jalapeño chip—taped out in just 9 months—outperforms Rubin on tokens/megawatt, though the competitive threat remains multi-year. SMH rejected near its declining 50-day MA (~600) post-NVDA fade.

bullets.title: Apple CEO transition: Tim Cook out, John Ternus in on Sept 1
bullets.body: Tim Cook's last day as Apple CEO is August 31; John Ternus officially takes over September 1. Under Cook's tenure Apple grew from $350B to ~$4.7T market cap (25.6% annualized). Apple also raised Apple TV+ and Apple One subscription prices for the second time in ~12 months.

bullets.title: AAPL as unintended AI beneficiary: OpenAI and Anthropic hoarding Mac hardware
bullets.body: OpenAI is hoarding tens of thousands of Mac Mini and Mac Studio units for reinforcement learning; Anthropic is renting Mac Minis from Amazon for similar AI tasks. Some customers are switching to NVIDIA DGX Spark due to long Apple lead times, but the volume going to Apple is substantial. One analyst called AAPL 'now an important AI company.'

bullets.title: SK Hynix considering Intel for next-gen HBM base die outsourcing
bullets.body: Multiple Korean media sources confirm SK Hynix is in discussions to outsource next-generation HBM base die production to Intel, representing a significant potential foundry win. SemiAnalysis noted SK Hynix had to redesign its base die, delaying HBM4 shipments for NVIDIA's Rubin platform; Samsung currently holds the best HBM4 technology.

bullets.title: TrendForce raises Q3 DRAM price forecast; DRAM/NAND costs surge 340% YoY in phones
bullets.body: TrendForce raised its Q3 PC DRAM price increase forecast to 18-23% QoQ from prior guidance of 15-20%. Separately, DRAM+NAND flash BOM costs for non-flagship smartphones are up 340% YoY, now exceeding the cost of premium chipsets—raising questions on whether memory cost shock is hitting consumer pricing.

bullets.title: Unimicron raided by Taiwan prosecutors over alleged China-origin substrate relabeling
bullets.body: Taiwan prosecutors raided Unimicron, a major ABF substrate supplier to NVDA, INTC, GOOGL, and AMZN, over allegations it relabeled China-made parts as Taiwan-origin. This raises supply chain integrity risk for AI chip packaging at a time when advanced substrate demand is tight.

bullets.title: GOOGL/AMZN book $152B+ in unrealized AI equity gains; autonomous vehicles cross 1M weekly rides
bullets.body: GOOGL booked $99B in mostly unrealized equity gains from SpaceX and Anthropic stakes in Q2 2026; AMZN recorded $53.4B from Anthropic markups. GOOGL, BIDU, and AMZN are collectively completing over 1M paid unsupervised autonomous rides per week without safety monitors, per one analyst.

bullets.title: META: antitrust case settled; AI infrastructure moat thesis gaining traction
bullets.body: META's social media lawsuit settled; one analyst argues even if its frontier AI lab fails, META can monetize its scarce compute assets. Meta is also testing robots for autonomous data center maintenance (cable swaps, server resets). META trades at 17.9x forward PE, with half of EPS attributable to Anthropic equity gains per some estimates.

bullets.title: Fabrinet (FN) building capacity to 2x+ revenue; COHR indifferent between NPO and CPO
bullets.body: Fabrinet exited Q4 at $1.316B revenue (+45% YoY) and management sees a path to $12.5-14B annual revenue capacity—more than double the current ~$5.3B run rate—driven by data-center demand. COHR says NPO and CPO carry roughly the same content for it, positioning the company to supply the full optical path under either architecture.

bullets.title: VIAV generating CPO testing revenue ahead of industry volume; Lumentum confirmed at ECOC 2026
bullets.body: VIAV is monetizing coherent pluggable optics (CPO) testing earlier than the rest of the industry, as CPO issues in a single optical channel can degrade entire package yield. Lumentum has two invited talks at ECOC 2026, validating the VCSEL thesis. TSM VP flagged that optical engine scaling is bottlenecked by lasers, connectors, and fiber—supply chain beneficiaries include LITE.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera Rubin 30x better throughput/MW vs GB300 on AgentX; AI PC pre-orders sold out
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis's AgentX benchmark shows Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x better throughput per megawatt vs. GB300 NVL72 on realistic agent workloads. Separately, Asustek and MSI's initial batches of Nvidia RTX Spark AI PCs completely sold out in pre-order; both vendors are requesting more chips from NVDA, with RTX Spark built on TSMC 3nm.

bullets.title: TSMC maintains 73% foundry market share; Q2 profit-sharing surges 54% YoY
bullets.body: TSMC's foundry market share held steady at 73% for the second consecutive quarter per one analyst. Its Q2 employee profit-sharing payout hit NT$36B (US$1.14B), up 50%+ YoY, with H1 2026 total bonus up 54.3%—reflecting AI-driven strength. Moody's also upgraded TSMC during the period.

bullets.title: Warsh Jackson Hole speech: Fed policy stance debate; Fedlock scores it as relatively dovish
bullets.body: While Warsh's speech was hawkish in absolute terms, Fedlock analysis scored it as still dovish relative to the broader FOMC. One Fed watcher predicts a 7-5 vote at the September 16 meeting; Chris Waller speaks September 3 and could be the swing vote. The market-implied September hike probability closed Friday at 58%.

bullets.title: Private Client cash at record low; stocks outperforming bonds by 66-year high margin
bullets.body: Bank of America Flow Show shows private clients at just 9% cash—lowest ever—while commodities vs. stocks trade at historically depressed levels. Separately, stocks are outperforming bonds over a 10-year horizon by the largest margin in 66 years, per chartbook data.

bullets.title: ABF substrate demand may be underappreciated; OSAT packaging deficit >20% by 2027
bullets.body: One analyst flagged that investors may be underestimating advanced ABF substrate scaling needs as AI clusters migrate across buildings and geographies. IC design insiders report OSAT providers warning of traditional packaging capacity deficits exceeding 20% by 2027—a potential near-term tailwind for AMKR.

bullets.title: US M2 hits record $23.22T; debt crosses $40T; Chamath warns 30Y at 6% = 'death spiral'
bullets.body: US M2 money supply reached a new all-time high of $23.22T. National debt crossed $40T, double the level from a decade ago, with interest costs up 15% YoY. Chamath Palihapitiya warned that 30-year yields reaching 6% would mark the 'beginning of a death spiral,' linking the AI infrastructure buildout to a new Grand Bargain era.
